verses.pali: “bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo ābādhiko ahosi dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: “Once upon a time, mendicants, Vepacitti, lord of titans, was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami gilānapucchako.
verses.english: So Sakka went to see him to ask after his illness.

verses.pali: Addasā kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: Vepacitti saw Sakka coming off in the distance,

verses.pali: ‘Na tāvāhaṁ vācemi, yāvāhaṁ, mārisa, asure paṭipucchāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘I can’t do that, good fellow, until I have consulted with the titans.’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo asure paṭipucchi:
verses.english: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, asked the titans,
‘Good fellows, may I teach the Sambari sorcery to Sakka, lord of gods?’

verses.pali: ‘Mā kho tvaṁ, mārisa, vācesi sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ sambarimāyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘Do not, good fellow, teach the Sambari sorcery to Sakka!’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: So Vepacitti addressed Sakka in verse:
into the terrible hell for a full century.’”
